To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of MPI and POSIX Threads provides an easy way to parallelize a medical imaging application.

a heterogenous cluster is a suitable platform for interactive visualization and segmentation of medical images and that the combination of MPI and POSIX threads is a suitable programming model for the implementation of such an application.

the proposed parallel system is a flexible, platform-indepen- dent tool for interactive segmentation and three-dimensional visualization of medical image data which can be distributed on heterogenous clusters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: (1) How to design an efficient and scalable parallel system for interactive image segmentation and visualization on heterogeneously configured parallel systems?
the design of a system which is able to process medical images on heterogenous parallel computers and to provide an intuitive user interface for interactive segmentation.
the development of a parallel system which is able to perform interactive segmentation and visualization on a cluster of symmetric multiprocessor computers using standardized libraries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented approach is able to provide a platform-independent, efficient and flexible parallel system for medical image processing and visualization.
the system is capable of handling large datasets and is highly scalable.
this system is a good basis to develop a parallel system for medical image processing and visualization which is distributed on heterogenous clusters and which can be used in clinical practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented system provides the user an easy to handle and efficient way to process and visualize three-dimensional medical images on a heterogenous network of workstations or PCs.
we are able to process and visualize large data sets in real-time on heterogenous clusters using a standardized software environment.
the system is able to segment a 512 x 512 x 64 image with 8 classes in 3.5 seconds on a 4 processor machine and 1.5 seconds on an 8 processor machine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a cluster of heterogeneous computers can be used to provide a powerful and flexible platform for image processing and visualization.
a heterogenous cluster can be used for interactive image segmentation and visualization without sacrificing performance or usability.
the design of a parallel system is possible without any knowledge of the underlying architecture.
